name: Joseph
charge: Refusing his master's wife: how can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
summary: Sold by his brothers, bought by Potiphar, tempted daily by his master's wife, Joseph refused, fled, and was jailed on her lie. The Lord was with him in the pit, in the prison, and in the palace, and he became the man through whom the whole house of Israel was kept alive.
offense: The refusal is not a single moment of resistance but a daily one: she spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not unto her. His stated ground is the one the case turns on. He names his master's trust first and then goes past it to the real bar, sinning against God, before Sinai, while serving as a Hebrew sold into Egypt (Genesis 39:8-10). Her repeated pressure did not make adultery less wicked. Genesis does not record a hearing at which he answered her accusation; it does record his later insistence that he had done nothing deserving imprisonment (Genesis 40:15). When she caught his garment, he left it in her hand and fled (Genesis 39:11-12). Escape from the sin cost him the appearance of innocence in her story, but he did not recover the garment by surrendering to the demand. In prison he continued serving, noticed the distress of the other prisoners, and directed the interpretation of their dreams to God (Genesis 40:4-8). Faithfulness continued before deliverance came.
judgment: The Lord was with Joseph in Potiphar's house and showed him mercy in prison (Genesis 39:2; Genesis 39:21-23). When he later stood before Pharaoh, he did not claim the interpretation of dreams as his own power: God would give the answer (Genesis 41:16). Favour followed him through service, confinement, and government; it was not measured merely by freedom from hardship. He was raised to govern the country that had bought him and became the means by which the family that sold him survived the famine (Genesis 41:56). His own verdict on the whole sequence is the centre of the case: ye thought evil against me (Genesis 50:20); but God meant it unto good.

verses.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.
And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
But he refused, and said unto his master’s wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.
But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.
The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.
And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:
Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.
Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.
He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:
Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:
Until the time that his word came: the word of the Lord tried him.
The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.
He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:
To bind his princes at his pleasure; and teach his senators wisdom.
When the righteous was sold, she forsook him not, but delivered him from sin: she went down with him into the pit,

And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.
Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.

entries.commentary: The Lord was with Joseph in his captivity, and his master saw that the Lord made all that he did to prosper; Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. The Most High deals with His people even in captivity and gives them compassion before them who carried them captive; the favor on Joseph is the pattern of that prayer.

His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, Lie with me; and he refused: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God? Adultery was known as sin from the beginning, long before Sinai. Abraham kept the commandments, statutes, and laws; and Abimelech rebuked Isaac because one of the people might have lain with his wife and brought guiltiness upon them. The nations themselves knew adultery brought guilt.

She spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not. Then she arranged the empty house, caught him by his garment, and he left his garment in her hand and fled. That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee; the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion. Joseph knew thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite.

When she saw he was fled, she lied and cried that the Hebrew came in to mock her, holding his garment as evidence. The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses.

When his master heard the words of his wife, his wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison. He did not seek understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man: he will not spare in the day of vengeance, nor regard any ransom.

But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison, and everything in the prison was committed to Joseph's hand. Everywhere Joseph went the favor followed, because the Most High was ordering his steps the whole way, so that Joseph would stand where he could save the whole house of Israel alive. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

After two full years Pharaoh dreamed: seven well favoured kine eaten up by seven ill favoured ones, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears blasted with the east wind. He saw different variations of the number seven, as the butler and the baker saw variations of three; the dream is a resemblance of one thing to another. His spirit was troubled, and none of the magicians and wise men of Egypt could interpret the dreams unto Pharaoh.

Pharaoh told Joseph he had heard he could understand a dream to interpret it, and Joseph gave all the praise to the Most High: it is not in me; God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace. The Most High reveals his secrets to his servants, and the secret of the Lord is with them that fear him. That is why the interpretation was with Joseph and not with the magicians of Egypt.

The dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice because the thing is established by God, and God will surely bring it to pass. Joseph did not stop at the interpretation; he gave the counsel: take up the fifth part of the land in the seven plenteous years and store it up, so Egypt could ration food through the years of famine. That shows what was on Joseph: he was wise, understanding, and diligent. A prudent man foresees the evil coming and makes preparation so he is not consumed in it; the simple pass on and are punished. There is treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spends it up; spending irrationally is a spirit of folly.

Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is? Israel has always been a wise and understanding people: Joseph in Egypt, Daniel in ancient Babylon, up until this day, a people responsible for many inventions and cunning arts. The children of Israel brought to Babylon were skilful in all wisdom, cunning in knowledge, understanding science, and able to stand in the king's palace to give counsel; and they were taught the tongue of the Chaldeans, for we have the capability to understand multiple languages as well.

Pharaoh set Joseph over his house and over all the land of Egypt; only in the throne was Pharaoh greater. Without Joseph no man lifted up his hand or foot in all Egypt: nothing moved unless Joseph decreed it. The Most High called for the famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph: sold for a servant, his feet hurt with fetters, laid in iron until the time that his word came; then the king loosed him and made him lord of his house, to bind his princes at his pleasure and teach his senators wisdom. Whether prince or common man, Joseph could bind any man in Egypt.

Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah and gave him Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On to wife. These heathens always like to change our names; that is one reason America is called spiritual Egypt, because they do the same thing that ancient Egypt did.

Joseph called the firstborn Manasseh, forgetting, for God had made him forget all his toil and all his father's house; and the second called he Ephraim, fruitful, for God had caused him to be fruitful in the land of his affliction. Ephraim was the second born, yet Ephraim possessed the kingship: the first king of the Northern Kingdom, Jeroboam, was of the tribe of Ephraim, not of Manasseh. Ephraim is the head tribe of the Northern Kingdom. Jacob set that in place. When Joseph saw his father lay his right hand upon Ephraim's head it displeased him, and he tried to move it to Manasseh's head; but Jacob refused and said, his younger brother shall be greater than he; and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.

The seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said. Another word for dearth is famine: no food, no sustenance to nourish the body. The dearth was in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread, because Joseph had stored up the seven years of plenty. All countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn.

Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept upon him, and kissed him, and commanded the physicians to embalm his father; forty days were fulfilled for the embalming, and the Egyptians mourned for Israel threescore and ten days.

Joseph asked leave of Pharaoh according to the oath his father made him swear, to bury him in the grave he had digged in the land of Canaan; and Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

All the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with Joseph and his brethren and his father's house, with chariots and horsemen, a very great company. The Canaanites saw the mourning in the floor of Atad and said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; wherefore the place was called Abelmizraim, which means the mourning of the Egyptians, beyond Jordan. The Israelites and the Egyptians were compared as looking like one people, because the Egyptians are black and the Israelites are black. The Bible dictionary defines Ham as the progenitor of the dark races, and Egypt was of Ham; the people sitting in that land today are not the true ancient Egyptians of the scriptures.

His sons did unto him according as he commanded them, and carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre; and Joseph returned into Egypt, he and his brethren, and all that went up with him.

When Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him; for they had sold him as a slave into Egypt. They sent a messenger pleading forgiveness and fell down before his face: Behold, we be thy servants. Joseph wept and answered, Fear not: for am I in the place of God? But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive. And he comforted them and spake kindly unto them, and nourished them and their little ones. Joseph had a real forgiving spirit. The lesson is to always be forgiving: sometimes people do evil against you, but the Most High means it unto good for you, so keep that spirit of forgiveness when people do certain things.

Joseph dwelt in Egypt and lived an hundred and ten years, and saw the children of Ephraim of the third generation; the children of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon Joseph's knees. Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel: God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence. So Joseph died, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt. That is why no Egyptologist can show you the mummy of Joseph, the tomb of so famous a man: when Israel fled out of the land of Egypt they took the bones of Joseph with them, according to that oath.

Give thanks unto the Most High, call upon His name, and make known His deeds among the people. Sing unto Him, glory in His holy name, and let the heart of them that seek Him rejoice; seek His face forevermore. Remember His marvelous works, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. The Bible tells us to remember our past. -

O seed of Abraham and children of Jacob His chosen: the Most High is our God and His judgments are in all the earth. He has remembered His covenant forever, the word commanded to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, confirmed to Jacob for a law and to Israel for an everlasting covenant. If Israel was to have an everlasting covenant, then the new covenant cannot suddenly involve all people. You must ask these questions of anyone who does not use the scriptures.

When they were few and strangers in the land, He suffered no man to wrong them and reproved kings for their sake: touch not mine anointed. He called a famine and sent a man before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant and bound with fetters until his word came to pass. The king loosed him and made him lord of his house and ruler of his substance, to bind his princes and teach his senators wisdom. Our forefather Joseph taught the Egyptians; those who boast in Egyptology forget our forefathers taught them. -

Israel came into Egypt and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham; He increased His people and made them stronger than their enemies, then turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate them. He sent Moses and Aaron who showed His signs and wonders in the land of Ham; He recounts the plagues of darkness, blood, frogs, flies, lice, hail, fire, and locusts. The locusts and caterpillars devoured all the herbs and fruit of the ground; this is the devourer, and the Most High promises to rebuke the devourer for the sake of a righteous nation. He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it. -

He brought Israel out with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among the tribes; look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses. He spread a cloud for a covering and fire for light, brought quails and the bread of heaven, and opened the rock so the waters gushed out in the dry place. He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America. -
